name: Arcturus Defense Solutions PolyBind PB-5
description:
The Arcturus Defense Solutions PB-5 PolyBind is a two-component reactive polymer adhesive delivered via a dual-chamber aerosol system. The two components — a polyurethane prepolymer and an accelerated moisture-cure catalyst — are stored separately within the canister and mixed at the nozzle tip at the moment of discharge. The resulting foam expands to approximately four times its liquid volume within two seconds of application and achieves a tensile bond strength sufficient to resist 180kg of separation force within eight seconds. Applied to a subject's feet, legs, or hands, the compound effectively immobilizes them by bonding to footwear, clothing, and any adjacent surface — floor, wall, or vehicle — with equal affinity. The set foam is resistant to tearing and requires either chemical solvent application or mechanical cutting to remove.

The PB-5 was developed for crowd control and perimeter security applications where conventional restraints cannot be applied quickly enough or in sufficient quantity. A single canister contains enough compound to produce three to four effective immobilization applications. The foam is chemically inert after curing and does not cause skin irritation or systemic toxicity in standard exposure; however, application over a subject's face or airway is explicitly prohibited in Arcturus's deployment guidelines due to asphyxiation risk from foam expansion in respiratory passages. The compound is soluble in Arcturus's proprietary PolyRelease PR-1 solvent, which takes approximately 90 seconds to work and is carried by operators for post-incident release of cooperative subjects.

The PB-5 has been adopted by several Tier 2 and 3 corporate security firms as a restraint alternative for situations where conventional zip-ties or handcuffs are impractical — large crowds, panicking individuals, subjects with augmented limbs that defeat standard restraints. Its effectiveness against augmented subjects is a particular selling point, as the polymer bonds to chrome and synthetic materials as readily as to fabric and concrete.
legality: Licensed — institutional purchase available to registered security contractors; individual purchase requires personal protection professional credential; use over airway or face is categorically prohibited
specifications: System type: dual-component reactive polyurethane foam Components: polyurethane prepolymer (Chamber A) / moisture-cure catalyst (Chamber B) Expansion ratio: 4:1 (liquid to cured foam) Initial cure time: 8 seconds (handling strength) Full cure time: 45 seconds Bond strength (full cure): 180kg separation resistance Applications per canister: 3–4 effective immobilization doses Chemical compatibility: bonds to fabric, chrome, concrete, polymer, glass Release agent: PolyRelease PR-1 (90-second dissolution) Lethality risk: asphyxiation if applied to face/airway Net weight: 340g Price: Φ480
tactical_use: Deployed to immobilize individuals at a distance without physical contact. The preferred application point is the lower legs and feet — a single burst anchors the subject to the floor within seconds. For augmented subjects with enhanced limb strength, application to multiple points simultaneously (both legs, or legs and one arm) increases restraint reliability. Operators carry PR-1 solvent for release of cooperative subjects. In perimeter security, the PB-5 is used to seal doorways and corridors by spraying across the floor, creating an adhesive zone.
cultural_context: In security circles, the PB-5 is called 'the curer' for its rapid-set properties. On the street, being 'ambered' — immobilized by PolyBind foam — has become a specific and humiliating term for a security encounter that went badly. The foam is visible, distinctive, and not quickly removed, meaning a 'cured' subject is publicly marked as having been restrained. There are accounts of security firms leaving individuals bonded in place for hours without deploying the PR-1 solvent, which is considered a significant abuse of the system.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone resident was found bonded to a wall in a transit corridor — dead from exposure, not from the foam itself. The PR-1 solvent that should have been used to release them is missing from the nearby security post log. No one has been assigned responsibility.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact aerosol canister with a distinctly industrial dual-chamber design. The body is cylindrical with a pronounced shoulder ridge marking the internal component separation. The nozzle assembly is oversized and heavily engineered, featuring dual ports and a visible mixing chamber. Overall impression is clinical and utilitarian—a tool built for rapid, repeatable deployment rather than elegance.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty for its size—340g creates noticeable heft in the hand. The weight distribution is slightly forward-biased due to the nozzle assembly and internal pressurization, making it feel purposeful and stable when gripped.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum pressure vessel (Tier 3 standard), polymer-reinforced nozzle assembly
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with subtle brushed aluminum highlights on the shoulder ridge. Pressure-tested certification marks are etched into the lower third. Minor scuff marks and handling wear are typical.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte gunmetal gray (primary) with safety-orange band around the nozzle assembly and black pressure-gauge window at the canister base
physical_description.grip_texture: Knurled polymer grip section in the lower half—textured for secure handling even with gloved hands or wet palms. The upper chamber is smooth bare aluminum.
distinctive_features: Dual-chamber visualization window showing internal liquid separation
Color-coded component indicators (blue label for Chamber A prepolymer, orange for Chamber B catalyst)
Pressure gauge with green/yellow/red safety zones
Integrated mixing chamber at nozzle tip with visible internal baffles
Arcturus Defense Solutions logo stamped in high-relief on the shoulder
Safety lever with tactile detents—requires deliberate squeeze to achieve full trigger travel
Expansion-foam residue (characteristic tan/beige dried polymer) visible on nozzle tip and crown edges from field use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions shield logo in high-relief on upper shoulder. Iron Point Ammunition subsidiary stamp on lower barrel. Serial number and pressure rating etched on base. Manufacturing date code (YYWW format) on side seam.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but clearly field-used. Pressure gauge shows recent operational status. Nozzle assembly shows residual polymer foam in micro-crevices—a sign of active deployment. Grip shows polishing from repeated gloved handling. No structural damage; all seals intact.
